output.summary: A perennial, spore-producing horsetail found across the temperate Northern Hemisphere, commonly forming dense colonies beside or within still or slow freshwater. Its green, jointed stems are mostly hollow and spread mainly through underground stems. Early spring shoots were historically eaten, including as a vegetable by poorer Romans, despite being unpalatable and not nutritious.
output.edibilityNote: Early spring shoots were historically eaten; poorer Romans sometimes used them as a vegetable despite their poor taste and low nutritional value.
